verdict: Pinnacle West earned $434M in a record-breaking Arizona summer — demand peaked at an all-time high of 9,166 megawatts — as customer growth and hot weather lifted electricity sales faster than higher depreciation and interest costs.

segments.name: Residential customers
segments.note: Electricity sold to Arizona homes by APS — the biggest source, boosted by a hotter-than-normal summer and 1.9% customer growth.

segments.name: Business customers
segments.note: Electricity sold to commercial and industrial customers — sales volumes rose 14.5% as factories and data centers expand in Arizona.

segments.name: Wholesale energy sales
segments.note: Surplus power sold to other utilities and markets.

segments.name: Transmission services
segments.note: Fees for moving other companies' power across APS's transmission lines.

opex.name: Operations & maintenance
opex.note: Running power plants and the grid day to day — crews, repairs and upkeep.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of power plants, lines and equipment over their useful lives — rising as APS builds for growth.

opex.name: Taxes other than income
opex.note: Mostly property taxes on plants and grid assets.

otherDetail: Other income of $21M — mostly the allowance for equity funds used during construction, a non-cash credit utilities earn on projects still being built — less net interest charges of $125M, for a net $104M drag.
footerNote: Adaptation for a utility: fuel and purchased power ($758M) is treated as the cost of revenue; operations & maintenance, depreciation, property and other taxes and other operating lines are shown as running costs, mirroring APS's income statement. Net income here is the consolidated $436M; $434M was attributable to common shareholders after $2M attributable to noncontrolling interests. Revenue split by customer type is from the 10-Q.

takeaways.title: Record demand, met reliably
takeaways.text: APS customers set an all-time peak demand record on August 2 and broke last year's record a dozen times during the quarter. The grid held up through one of the more active monsoon seasons in years.

takeaways.title: Growth is the story
takeaways.text: Weather-normalized electricity sales grew 9.5% and the customer count rose 1.8%. APS expects customers' annual electricity needs to more than double by 2041, and its new long-term plan requires extra-large new users to pay for the infrastructure they need.

takeaways.title: Guidance raised, bills credited
takeaways.text: Pinnacle West raised its full-year 2026 EPS guidance to $5.05–$5.25. Separately, APS is returning over $33M in bill credits this November — about $14 off a typical home's bill — plus $5M of hardship assistance funded by the company.
